2. Identify and remove the single record whose crime-rate value is missing; keep it out of every later calculation (data_points_used = 32).  
3. Build an adjacency dictionary {borough: [neighbor1, neighbor2, …]}. If a neighbor was the one row with a missing value, simply exclude that neighbor from every local-area sum in which it would have appeared.  
4. For every remaining borough i:  
   a. Form the local area Ωᵢ = {i + all valid neighbors of i}.  
   b. Compute Sᵢ = sum of crime-rate values across Ωᵢ.  
5. Collect all Sᵢ values (one per borough still in the data set). Let 𝜇 = mean(Sᵢ) and σ = std. dev.(Sᵢ).  
6. For each borough i, calculate zᵢ = (Sᵢ – 𝜇)/σ.  
7. Classify significance:  
   • zᵢ > +1.96 → HOT at 95% (zᵢ > +2.576 → HOT at 99%).  
   • zᵢ < –1.96 → COLD at 95% (zᵢ < –2.576 → COLD at 99%).  
8. Exclude any borough whose own crime-rate was missing (already removed) from being reported, even if its Sᵢ was calculable through neighbors.  
9. Assemble a list such as “BoroughName (HOT, z = <real number>)” or “(COLD, z = <real number>)” for every statistically significant borough.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Paths supplied in the prompt
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2015.csv"
ADJ_PATH  = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

# 1. Load data
crime_df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)         # columns: borough, crime_rate_value
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)          # columns: borough, neighbor

# 2. Drop rows whose crime value is missing
crime_df = crime_df.dropna(subset=["crime_rate_value"]).reset_index(drop=True)

# dictionary: borough -> crime value
crime_values = dict(zip(crime_df["borough"], crime_df["crime_rate_value"]))

# 3. Build adjacency list – exclude missing-value boroughs from every list
valid_boroughs = set(crime_values.keys())

adjacency = {b: set() for b in valid_boroughs}
for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b, n = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    if b in valid_boroughs and n in valid_boroughs:   # ignore any side involving the missing borough
        adjacency[b].add(n)

# 4. Compute the local-area sum S_i  (borough + all its neighbors)
local_sums = {}
for b in valid_boroughs:
    neighbours = adjacency.get(b, set())
    group      = {b} | neighbours
    # keep only boroughs that still have a numeric crime value
    group      = [g for g in group if g in crime_values]
    local_sums[b] = sum(crime_values[g] for g in group)

# 5. Citywide distribution of the local sums
S_vals = np.array(list(local_sums.values()))
mu     = S_vals.mean()
sigma  = S_vals.std(ddof=0)     # population std.  Using 0 so the z-formula matches a true z.
# guard against division by zero, though sigma shouldn't be zero in real data
if sigma == 0:
    raise ValueError("Standard deviation of local sums is zero; cannot compute z-scores.")

# 6. z-score for every borough
z_scores = {b: (local_sums[b] - mu)/sigma for b in local_sums}

# 7. Identify statistically significant hot/cold spots
hotcold = {}
for b, z in z_scores.items():
    if z > 2.576:            # 99% HOT
        hotcold[b] = ("HOT", z)
    elif z > 1.96:           # 95% HOT
        hotcold[b] = ("HOT", z)
    elif z < -2.576:         # 99% COLD
        hotcold[b] = ("COLD", z)
    elif z < -1.96:          # 95% COLD
        hotcold[b] = ("COLD", z)

# 8. Prepare output
data_points_used = len(valid_boroughs)

if hotcold:
    results = [f"{b} ({label}, z={z:.4f})" for b, (label, z) in sorted(hotcold.items())]
    print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
